references.text: Abram divided the animals and placed the pieces opposite each other—the direct background for the flaming torch that passed between the pieces in v.17.
God's presence as a pillar of fire by night and a pillar of cloud by day to lead the Israelites resembles the flaming torch and smoke that manifested God's presence in the covenant with Abram.
The smoke and fire on Mount Sinai when the Lord came down recall the smoke and flaming torch in God's covenant-making with Abram.
Jeremiah explicitly refers to the covenant ritual of walking between the pieces of a calf—a direct parallel to the ceremony in Gen 15:17.
The Lord's pillar of fire that went before Israel's camp at night can be compared to the flaming torch that passed between the animal pieces in God's covenant with Abram.
The means of the new covenant through blood, mentioned in Hebrews, are connected to the covenant-making God confirmed with Abram through the sacrificial animals.
The deep sleep and terror that fell upon Abram as the sun went down is the immediate context for the darkness and God's fire manifestation in v.17.
Fire rose from the rock and consumed the offering Gideon had laid out—a parallel to God's fire confirming his presence and acceptance of the sacrifice.
